review.summary: Jones’s 2008 letter interpreted a sparse dated California record as consistent with Younger Dryas disruption; a contemporary reanalysis directly disputed the demographic inference.
review.limitations: Historical dispute based on then-available dates; neither a dated-record gap nor a probability sum directly counts people or proves an extraterrestrial cause.
review.discussion: Collard and colleagues reanalyzed 73 Californian dates and found neither Jones’s reconstructed decline nor the major post-12900 cal BP drop predicted by the impact hypothesis. Erosion, sampling and later discoveries also limit use of a 2008 absence claim today.

corrections.correction: Regional archaeological persistence, genetic continuity and continuous use of one site are different claims. Neither a DNA series nor >100 sites establishes no occupational breaks.
7400 to 200 cal BP spans about 7200 years; do not describe it as a 7400-year uninterrupted lineage. Substantial continuity coexists with later admixture.
Author correction reassigns erroneous mitochondrial C5b calls to C1b/C1c; use corrected materials.
La Playa lies in Sonora, Mexico, and the 2023 source uses Cienega 2800–1900 cal BP. Preserve differing regional period conventions.
Indistinguishable directions permit related firing windows, not proof of a single simultaneous intentional fire or permanent site abandonment.
Bonneville association, San Diego noncorrelation and San Carlos village-adaptation interpretation apply to different scales and settings. Do not collapse them into one causal rule.
Primary abstract supports a coalescence interpretation; it does not establish Medieval Climatic Anomaly causation.
Jones's disruption claim received a direct contrary radiocarbon reanalysis; mark explicit dispute rather than present a sparse record as proof of depopulation.
Western Stemmed and Clovis labels identify technologies, not automatically bounded peoples or migration routes.
